workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§189–190
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§189–190: Tayang's Mother, the Quivers and the Naiman Message
part: §§189–190 — Tayang's Mother, the Quivers and the Naiman Message
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§189–190, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Two sections on the Naiman side of the war. In §189 Tayang Qan's mother Kürbesü has Wang Qan's severed head brought, sets it on a white felt and makes offerings to it; the head laughs, Tayang smashes it, and the old speeches follow: Kökse'ü-Sabraq calls it unfit, words of Inancha-Bilge (read as Tayang's father) are quoted against him, and Tayang speaks of the few Mongols in the east and of taking their quivers, while his mother, scornful of the Mongols' smell, would take only their daughters-in-law and daughters. §190 sends the message on: Tayang asks the Önggüd Alaqush-Digit-Quri to be his right hand against the Mongols; Alaqush refuses and sends his envoy Juqunan to Chinggis Qahan with a warning, which reaches him at a circle hunt. The war council that follows, with Ödchigin Noyan and Belgütei, turns on the lean geldings and on a quiver taken by a follower, and ends with Belgütei's call to mount. The grammar to watch is the nested quotation (several speeches inside speeches, with Shiratori's marks only partly closing), the causatives in -ġül-, and a run of rhetorical questions in -užai. Several lines are hard and the notes say so; two words, torluγ and torulmiši, have no Ming gloss at all. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori; the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Naiman-u Tajaṅ Qān-(n)u eke Kürbesü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝的]
Kürbesü, a woman's name (the word also exists as the conditional of kür- 'reach', but the Ming marks a name) [人名]

sentences.l: Naiman's Tajaṅ Qān's mother Kürbesü, speaking:
sentences.i: Kürbesü, mother of Tayang Qan of the Naiman, said:
sentences.n: The colon after ügülerün ('when speaking', -rün) opens a speech. Naiman-u Tajaṅ Qān-(n)u eke is a genitive chain read from the right: 'mother of Tayang Qan of the Naiman'. Kürbesü is taken as a woman's name because the Ming marks it 人名, though the same letters also spell the conditional of kür- 'reach'; the English spelling Kürbesü is mine. The (n) of Qān-(n)u is Shiratori's, as in the other glossed forms.

sentences.t: "Waṅ-Qān erten-ü ötögü jeke qān büleġe.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' with qan) [人名]
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: "Waṅ-Qān, of former time old great qan, was.
sentences.i: "Wang Qan was the old great qan of former times.
sentences.n: The print puts a quotation mark before Waṅ-Qān and closes it only after bida in the next unit, so these are Kürbesü's words. In the English of this part, speeches are in double quotation marks and a speech inside a speech in single ones; where the print leaves a mark out I supply it and say so. erten-ü is 'of former time' (Ming 在前的) and works as an adjective by its genitive. büleġe is the past of bü- 'be'; no copula is supplied in the literal line.

sentences.t: Teriġü in-ü abčiradqun mün böġesü taija bida" keġežü

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

words.reading: 阿卜赤舌剌惕中渾 abčiradqun

morph.gloss: imperative, second person plural: you (all) … (Ming 您)
to make an offering (stem inferred from the Ming 祭祀) [祭祀咱]

sentences.l: Head his bring-you(pl), that very if-it-be, sacrifice-let-us we," saying,
sentences.i: Bring his head. If that is so, let us make an offering to it," she said,
sentences.n: abčiradqun carries the Ming 您 'you' (plural): an imperative to several people, with -qun as the ending (the same ending returns in saγ̇aγ̇ulqun and niγ̇udqun; the -d before it I take as a plural mark, uncertain). taija is the hortative 'let us', and bida repeats 'we' (Ming 咱, the inclusive we). mün böġesü is 'if it is just so'; I read it as 'if that is so' (that Wang Qan was a great qan), leaving the antecedent open; 'if it is indeed he' is the other reading. keġežü 'saying' closes the quotation, which the print opens before Waṅ-Qān in the unit above.

sentences.t: Qori-Sübeči-dür elči iležü.

words.reading: 中豁舌里-速別赤-突︀舌兒 Qori-Sübeči-dür

glyphs.s: 中豁舌里-速別赤-突︀舌兒

morph.gloss: Qori-Sübechi, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.l: Qori-Sübeči-to envoy sending.
sentences.i: She sent an envoy to Qori-Sübechi.
sentences.n: -dür is the dative-locative 'to' (Ming 行). The full stop falls after the converb iležü 'sending', so the sentence is carried by a converb; the Ming 敎去着 'causing to go' agrees. The subject is not repeated; it is Kürbesü.

sentences.t: teriġü in-ü hoγtolžu abčiraγ̇ulžu tanižu čaγan toloγ deġere talbižu

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to cut off (stem inferred from the Ming 斷) [割斷着]

words.reading: 阿卜赤舌剌兀勒周 abčiraγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: felt, a large felt (Ming 大氊; sense inferred) [大氊]

sentences.l: Head his cutting-off, causing-to-bring, recognising, white felt on setting,
sentences.i: His head cut off, she had it brought; she knew it and set it on a white felt,
sentences.n: A long chain of converbs in -žu ('-ing'), which I break in three: here hoγtolžu, abčiraγ̇ulžu, tanižu, talbižu; then the daughters-in-law (next unit); then the finite verb taižuγ̇ui. Subjects are not marked. A chain in -žu normally keeps one subject, so I take Kürbesü as the subject throughout (abčiraγ̇ulžu is causative, 'had it brought'). hoγtolžu 'cutting off' I leave without an agent in the English: the Ming does not say who cut the head, though Kökse'ü-Sabraq's reproach later in this section ('you cut off … and brought') puts the cutting on her side. The reflexive -jen in the next unit shows that Kürbesü is the subject by then. toloγ (Ming 大氊, 'large felt') I take as a felt mat or rug; the stem hoγtol- is inferred from the Ming 斷 'cut'.

sentences.t: berined(i)-jen berileġülžü ötögleġülžü quγ̇urdaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: daughter-in-law (n-stem, berine- before -d) [媳婦(每)自的(行)]
Shiratori's bracketed (i) before the reflexive (perhaps the accusative -i; Ming 行)
to do a daughter-in-law's duty (stem inferred from the Ming 媳婦的禮) [敎媳婦的禮行着]
to offer the cup (stem inferred from the Ming 喝盞) [敎喝︀盞着]

words.reading: 中忽兀舌兒荅兀勒周 quγ̇urdaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: to pluck, strum (stem inferred from the Ming 彈) [敎彈着]

sentences.l: Daughters-in-law-her-own bride's-duty-causing, cup-offering-causing, strumming-causing,
sentences.i: she had her own daughters-in-law perform a daughter-in-law's courtesies, offer the cup, and strum,
sentences.n: Three causatives (-ġül-, 'make … do') in a row, each ending in the converb -žu/-žü. The Ming gives the sense of each, and I inferred all three stems: berile- from 媳婦的禮 'a daughter-in-law's courtesy', ötögle- from 喝盞 'drink the cup' (to offer the toast), quγ̇urda- from 彈 'pluck, strum'. What is strummed is not said (the Ming 彈 names no instrument). berined(i)-jen: berin 'daughter-in-law' (stem berine-), plural -d, Shiratori's bracketed (i), and the reflexive -jen 'her own' (Ming 自的行). Compare the possessive/reflexive endings -jan/-jen in the glossary.

sentences.t: ajaγa barižu taižuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: to take hold of, grasp [拿着]
to make an offering [祭祀了有]

sentences.l: Cup taking-hold, offered-sacrifice.
sentences.i: Holding the cup, she made the offering.
sentences.n: The finite verb at last: taižuγ̇ui, from tai- 'make an offering' (inferred from the Ming 祭祀) with the narrative past -žuγ̇ui (Ming 了有). The chain that began at 'Teriġü in-ü hoγtolžu' ends here.

sentences.t: Tende teriġün tein taiγdarun inežüġü.

morph.gloss: to make an offering [被祭祀時]

sentences.l: There head so being-offered-to-when laughed.
sentences.i: Then, as the head was thus being offered to, it laughed.
sentences.n: The subject is the head (teriġün, here with a final -n; the Ming glosses both spellings 頭). taiγdarun is tai- + passive -γda- + the converb of time -run: 'when it was offered to' (Ming 被祭祀時). inežüġü (Ming 咲有來; 咲 is a variant of 笑) is 'laughed'; the Ming does not say whether it is a smile.

sentences.t: Ineġebe keġen Tajaṅ Qān kebgerü gečikileġüilžüġüi.

morph.gloss: to laugh (Ming 咲; a variant of ine-, form uncertain) [咲了]
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
to break to pieces (stem inferred from the Ming 破碎) [破碎]

words.reading: 格赤乞列兀(勒)主爲 gečikileġüilžüġüi

morph.gloss: to trample (Ming 踐踏; stem uncertain) [踐踏了]
causative (printed -ġüil-; the Han 兀(勒) is ġü + a bracketed l, so I read the usual -ġül-; the Ming 踐踏了 shows no causative sense; uncertain)

sentences.l: 'It laughed!' saying, Tajaṅ Qān smashing, trampled.
sentences.i: Saying "It laughed!", Tayang Qan smashed it to pieces and trampled it.
sentences.n: keġen, from keġe- 'say', is the converb that closes a quotation; the quotation here is the single word Ineġebe and has no marks in the print. kebgerü (Ming 破碎) and the finite gečikileġüilžüġüi (Ming 踐踏了, 'trampled') are both uncertain in stem. The long form is printed -ġüil-, but the Han 兀(勒) is ġü with a bracketed l, the causative -ġül- as in abčiraγ̇ulžu (兀勒); so I read -ġül- and take the i as a slip of the romanization (uncertain). The Ming 踐踏了 shows no 'cause', so the sense is plain 'trampled'. The Ming leaves the object unstated; it is the head.

sentences.t: Tende Kögseġü-Sabraγ ügüležüġü.

words.reading: 可克薛兀-撒(卜)舌剌黑 Kögseġü-Sabraγ

morph.gloss: Kökse'ü-Sabraq, a Naiman man's name [人名]

sentences.l: There Kögseġü-Sabraγ spoke.
sentences.i: Then Kökse'ü-Sabraq spoke.
sentences.n: ügüležüġü is the narrative past -žüġü of ügüle- 'speak' (Ming 說了有). The quotation that follows is long and opens with a mark before Ükügsen in the next unit; it closes only after bi in the unit ending keġegdežü.

sentences.t: "Ükügsen qān küġün-ü teriġün in-ü ta kü hoγtolžu abčirad

morph.gloss: past participle: the one who has died
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to cut off (stem inferred from the Ming 斷) [割斷着]
verb ending going with a plural subject (here ta), as in ügüled and kebgerid; uncertain, a converb "having …" is the other reading

sentences.l: "Dead qan, person's head, his, you indeed cutting-off, brought-ye,
sentences.i: "You cut off the head of a dead qan, a man, and brought it,
sentences.n: ükügsen qān küġün-ü: 'dead qan, of a man', the three words standing before teriġün in-ü 'head, his'; I read it as 'the head of a man, a dead qan'. ta is the polite plural 'you' (Ming 您) and kü 'indeed' (Ming 也, 'also'). abčirad has the same -d as kebgerid and ügüled, which goes with ta (uncertain; a converb 'having brought' is the other reading, but this clause stands alone). A sentence carried over two units: this one is the first half. The print opens Kökse'ü-Sabraq's speech here and closes it after bi, at the end of the speech.

sentences.t: nögöġete ta kü kebgerid jaγ̇un žokiqui.

morph.gloss: adverbial ending (uncertain): for the second time
to break to pieces (stem inferred from the Ming 破碎; compare kebgerü) [敎碎了]
ending of uncertain form; with ta, as in abčirad and ügüled, perhaps the plural-subject -d with a linking i

sentences.l: Second-time you indeed smashing: what fitting?
sentences.i: and you smashed it a second time. What is fitting in that?
sentences.n: kebgerid (Ming 敎碎了, 'caused to be smashed') I take from the same stem as kebgerü above (the stem is inferred from the Ming); the ending -id is not clear, and with ta it is probably the same plural-subject -d as in abčirad (uncertain). žokiqui is the participle of žoki- 'to suit': jaγ̇un žokiqui, 'what is fitting?', is a rhetorical 'is that proper?'. nögöġete (Ming 第二次) I analyse as nögöġe 'second' with an adverbial -te.

sentences.t: Noγan-u bidan-u qučaqui daγ̇un maγ̇ui bolbi.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (the stem takes -n- before the ending)
genitive: of (the stem takes -n- before the ending)
to bark (stem inferred from the Ming 吠) [吠的]

sentences.l: Dogs of-us barking sound bad became.
sentences.i: The barking of our dogs has turned bad.
sentences.n: Possessors come first: noγan-u bidan-u qučaqui daγ̇un, 'of the dogs, of us, barking sound', with the two genitives both depending on daγ̇un. bidan-u is the inclusive 'our'. qučaqui is the participle of an inferred quča- 'bark' (Ming 吠的). The dogs' changed voice is taken as an omen; the Ming only says 歹 'bad'.

sentences.t: Inanča-Bilge Qān ügüleleġe.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Inanča-Bilge Qān had said.
sentences.i: Inancha-Bilge Qan had said:
sentences.n: A quotation inside Kökse'ü-Sabraq's speech; Shiratori marks neither its opening nor its end. The text never says who Inancha-Bilge is, but what he says ('my son', 'I had this Tayang born') makes him Tayang's father. -leġe is the past of ügüle-, 'had said' (Ming 說來).

sentences.t: Eme žalaγ̇ui; ere bi ötölbe.
sentences.l: Wife young; husband I grew-old.
sentences.i: 'The wife is young; I, the husband, have grown old.
sentences.n: eme can be 'woman' or 'wife'; the Ming 婦人 gives 'woman', and with ere 'husband' the pair is read as husband and wife. No copula in the literal line (žalaγ̇ui is simply 'young'); ötölbe is ötöl- 'grow old' with the past -be. The semicolon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: Ene Tajaṅ-ji elbesü-ġer töreġülüleġe.

morph.gloss: prayer, invocation (Ming 禱神 'pray to the spirits'; sense inferred) [(禱神︀依着)]

sentences.l: This Tajaṅ(acc) prayer-by caused-to-be-born-had.
sentences.i: I had this Tayang born by prayer.
sentences.n: töreġülüleġe is töre- 'be born' with the causative -ġül-: 'caused to be born', i.e. fathered or brought into being. The Ming glosses elbesü-ġer with a bracket, (禱神依着) 'relying on prayer to the spirits'; that is the glossator's own expansion, so elbesü is a guess from it and -ġer is the instrumental 'by means of'.

sentences.t: Ai torluγ töregsen köġün min-u torulmiši olon doromžin maγ̇ui ulus min-u asaražu barin čidaqu-ju keġeleġe.

morph.gloss: (sense unknown: the Ming gives no gloss; it stands beside a ruler or a son as an epithet)
I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun
(sense unknown: the Ming gives no gloss)
lowly, of low rank (Ming 下等) [下等]
I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun
to lift up, raise (stem inferred from the Ming 擡擧) [擡擧着]

sentences.l: Alas! torluγ born son my, torulmiši many lowly bad people my, lifting-up, holding able-?, had-said.
sentences.i: Alas! My son, born torluγ, will he be able to lift up and hold my many torulmiši, lowly, bad people?' he had said.
sentences.n: Two words in this unit, torluγ and torulmiši, have no Ming gloss at all (the glossator left them blank), and I cannot supply a meaning; I leave them in the English. torluγ comes again at Qān min-u torluγ Tajaṅ below and in §190; it behaves like an epithet of Tayang. Whether torulmiši belongs with ulus 'people' is a guess from word order. The syntax after that is clear: asaražu barin, 'lifting, holding' (Ming 擡擧着 把), then čidaqu-ju, 'able?' with the question particle (Ming 能的麽). keġeleġe 'had said' ends the quotation within Kökse'ü-Sabraq's speech, which I take as Inancha-Bilge's; the print does not say where it ends. A long unit, but I find no clean place to break it.

sentences.t: Edöġe noγan-u daγ̇un idüreküi qučal qučamui.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (the stem takes -n- before the ending)
to draw near (stem inferred from the Ming 將近) [將近的]
bark, barking (bare stem or noun; Ming 吠) [吠]

sentences.l: Now dog's sound nearing, bark barks.
sentences.i: Now the dogs' sound is drawing near, bark upon bark.
sentences.n: idüreküi (Ming 將近的, 'about to reach') is a participle; the stem idüre- is inferred. qučal qučamui repeats one verb, the bare stem and then the present -mui (Ming 吠 吠有): 'barks and barks'. The repetition is a pattern, like žüg žüg in §186. Whether it is the dogs' sound that draws near or they that bark nearer, the grammar allows both.

sentences.t: Qatun-(n)u bidan-u Kürbesü-jin žasaγ qurča bolbi.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, a qan's wife [娘子 的]
genitive: of (the stem takes -n- before the ending)
Kürbesü, a woman's name [人名 的]

sentences.l: Lady's, of-us, Kürbesü's rule sharp became.
sentences.i: The rule of our Lady, Kürbesü, has grown keen.
sentences.n: All three genitives, qatun-(n)u 'of the lady', bidan-u 'of us', Kürbesü-jin 'of Kürbesü', depend on žasaγ 'law, rule' (Ming 法度); -jin is the genitive after a vowel. qurča is Ming 鋒利, 'sharp-edged', hence 'keen' or 'severe'. The speaker is not named; I read it, with what follows, as part of the long speech Kökse'ü-Sabraq is making.

sentences.t: Qān min-u torluγ Tajaṅ žöġölen bijü.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun
(sense unknown: the Ming gives no gloss; it stands beside a ruler or a son as an epithet)
soft, gentle, weak (Ming 柔弱) [柔弱]

sentences.l: Qān my torluγ Tajaṅ soft is.
sentences.i: My Qan, torluγ Tayang, is soft.
sentences.n: Qān min-u: 'qan, mine'; the genitive min-u follows its noun. torluγ again has no Ming gloss, as in Inancha-Bilge's words above. žöġölen is Ming 柔弱 'soft, weak'; bijü is the present of bü- 'be'.

sentences.t: Či šibaγ̇ulaqu abalaqu qojar-ača buši sedkil erdem ügei bi" keġegdežü

morph.gloss: to hunt with hawks (stem inferred from the Ming 放鷹) [放鷹的]
to hunt, drive game (stem inferred from the Ming 打獵) [打獵的]
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: You hawking, hunting, two-from other heart, skill without are," being-told,
sentences.i: Apart from those two, hawking and hunting, you have no other thought or skill," so he was told.
sentences.n: qojar-ača, 'from the two' (ablative), with buši 'other', gives 'apart from the two (hawking and hunting)'. sedkil erdem ügei, 'heart, skill, without': two nouns with one ügei. The closing quotation mark sits after bi. keġegdežü is keġe- 'say' + passive -gde- + the converb: 'being told', whose subject is Tayang in the next unit, so the whole of Kökse'ü-Sabraq's speech, from Ükügsen, is spoken to him.

sentences.t: tende Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: There Tajaṅ Qān, speaking:
sentences.i: Then Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: tende 'there, then'; ügülerün 'speaking' opens the speech. The subject of the preceding passive keġegdežü is Tajaṅ Qān.

sentences.t: Ene dorona čüġeked Monγol bi keġegdemüi.

morph.gloss: east, on the east side [東行]
the Mongols (the Ming writes 達達, 'Tatars') [達達]
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: These east few Mongols are, is-said.
sentences.i: "It is said that there are a few Mongols here in the east.
sentences.n: keġegdemüi is the passive-present 'is said', so hearsay. čüġeked is čüġeke(n) 'few' with the plural -d (Ming 少的每). The Ming glosses Monγol as 達達 (the Ming's usual word for the Mongols; I keep Mongols). bi (Ming 有) is the short copula, left out of the literal line. Almost the same words open the message to Alaqush in §190.

sentences.t: Tede irgen ötökü jeke erten-ü Waṅ-Qān-(n)i qor(i)-jar(i)-jan ajuγ̇ulžu daižiγ̇ulžu üküġülbe.

words.reading: 中豁舌里-牙舌里-顏 qor(i)-jar(i)-jan

morph.gloss: instrumental: by means of (the token jar(i) of the glossary; the Ming 自的行 belongs to the reflexive -jan; uncertain)
to fear (stem inferred from the Ming 怕) [敎怕着]
to turn against, rebel (stem inferred from the Ming 反) [反了着]

sentences.l: Those people, old great of-former-time Waṅ-Qān(acc), by-own-quiver, frightening, making-rebel, caused-to-die.
sentences.i: Those people, with their own quiver, frightened old Wang Qan of former times, made him rebel, and caused his death.
sentences.n: A chain of two causative converbs (ajuγ̇ulžu, daižiγ̇ulžu) and a finite causative (üküġülbe, 'caused to die'), so each is a 'make' form: stems aju- 'fear' and daiži- 'rebel' are inferred from the Ming 怕 and 反. The word is qor(i)-jar(i)-jan: qor 'quiver' (Ming 箭筒), Shiratori's linking (i), -jar (the instrumental of the glossary; the Ming 自的行 belongs to the reflexive at the end), another (i), and -jan 'one's own'. So 'by their own quiver', 'their' being the subject, tede irgen; but the reflexive could also point at Wang Qan, the object. What 'by quiver' means the text does not say: it may be the means, or the armed men themselves. daižiγ̇ul- is Ming 反了, 'turned, rebelled', so 'made him rebel' (not 'set against').

sentences.t: Edöġe mün Qān bolsu keġen aqun-u tede.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
to be (Ming 存心有的 'keeping in mind'; analysis uncertain) [存心有的]

sentences.l: Now just Qān let-him-be saying, keeping-in-mind, those.
sentences.i: Now those people keep it in mind, saying, 'Let him alone be Qan.'
sentences.n: Hard to be sure. mün (Ming 只他, 'only he, that very man') + Qān bolsu (optative -su, 'let him be') + keġen 'saying' (closing the thought), then aqun-u, Ming 存心有的, 'those who keep it in mind', and tede 'those'. I read aqun-u as a- 'be' + the participle ending -qun (the glossary has aqun for Ming 有的, 'being') + -u; 'keeping it in mind' is the Ming's gloss, not a stem. The glossary's earlier aqun-u (Ming 莫不有, 'perhaps') has a different gloss for the same spelling, and I cannot tell whether it is the same word. Who 'him' is, the text does not say here.

sentences.t: Teṅgeri deġere naran sara qojar gereten gegeġen boltuγai" keġen

morph.gloss: light (Ming 光; stem inferred) [光有的(每)]

sentences.l: Heaven above sun, moon, two light-having, bright let-it-be," saying,
sentences.i: Saying, 'Let the sun and the moon, the two, be bright with their light in Heaven above,'
sentences.n: The Ming reads 天上日月兩箇光有的明做者麽道: 'in Heaven the sun and moon, two, having light, may they be bright, saying'. gereten (Ming 光有的(每)) is 'those having light', from an inferred gere 'light' plus a possessive plural; boltuγai is the optative 'may it be'. keġen is the converb 'saying'; who says it I cannot tell, so I give it as a saying quoted by Tayang, in single marks inside his speech. The print closes a quotation after boltuγai and again after abčiraja three units on, and opens neither; I take the second as the end of Tayang's whole speech (which I open at 'It is said that there are a few Mongols') and the first as the end of this inner saying, uncertain. The logic completes in the next two units: the sky has two lights, and the earth cannot have two sovereigns.

sentences.t: naran sara qojar bi-že.
sentences.l: Sun, moon, two are-indeed.
sentences.i: the sun and the moon are two.
sentences.n: bi-že is bi 'is' with -že 'indeed' (Ming 有也者, 'it is so, indeed'). Read with the unit before, it is the premise of the question that follows: the sun and the moon are two in the sky.

sentences.t: Γažar deġere qojar qād ker bolqu.
sentences.l: Earth on, two sovereigns, how become?
sentences.i: How can there be two sovereigns on the earth?
sentences.n: qād is the contracted plural of qaγan, 'sovereigns' (house rendering). bolqu is the participle of bol- 'be' (Ming 做) used as a question with ker 'how'. γažar deġere, 'on the earth', answers teṅgeri deġere 'in Heaven' above.

sentences.t: Bida ögčü tedeked Monγol-i abčiraja" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: further plural ending (uncertain; Ming 那些 'those few')

sentences.l: We giving, those Mongols(acc) let-us-bring," saying.
sentences.i: Let us bring those Mongols along," he said.
sentences.n: bida ögčü: 'we, giving' (Ming 咱 與着). I cannot say what is given, nor to whom, and I leave ögčü out of the English; it may mark a command given, or a benefactive 'for us'. abčiraja is abčira- 'bring' with the hortative -ja (Ming 將來咱); monγol-i is the accusative. Tayang is the speaker.

sentences.t: Teġün-dür eke in-ü Kürbesü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
Kürbesü, a woman's name (the word also exists as the conditional of kür- 'reach', but the Ming marks a name) [人名]

sentences.l: That-at mother his Kürbesü, speaking:
sentences.i: Then his mother Kürbesü said:
sentences.n: teġün-dür is the oblique of tere + -dür, 'thereupon' (Ming 那的裏). eke in-ü is 'mother, his': the possessive in-ü follows its noun. Kürbesü speaks again.

sentences.t: "Jekiġü-že tedeġer-i Monγol irgen hünür maγ̇utan qubčasu baratutan büleġe.

morph.gloss: those (collective plural of tere) [那(的)每行]
the Mongols (the Ming writes 達達, 'Tatars') [達達]
dark, dim (Ming 暗; stem inferred) [暗(有的每)]

sentences.l: "What-to-do-indeed? Those(acc) Mongol people, smell bad-having, clothes dark-having, were.
sentences.i: "What is to be done with those Mongol people? They smelled foul, and their clothes were dark.
sentences.n: jekiġü-že (Ming 要做甚麽) is jaki- 'do what' with a participle and -že: 'what is to be done?'; with the accusative tedeġer-i it asks 'what is to be done with them?', a rhetorical 'why bother?'. tedeġer-i is a collective 'those', accusative. maγ̇utan and baratutan both end in -tan, Ming 有的每 'those having': 'the ill-smelling', 'the dark-clothed'; I take -tan as a possessive plural, uncertain. hünür (Ming 氣) 'smell' is paired with maγ̇u 'bad'; baratu is Ming 暗 'dark, dim', here 'dark'. büleġe is the past, 'were'.

sentences.t: Aṅgida qolo büžü bütügei.
sentences.l: Apart far being, let-them-be.
sentences.i: Let them stay far off, elsewhere.
sentences.n: bütügei is bü- 'be' with the optative -tügei: 'let them be'; the Ming glosses 有者. The glossary's earlier bütügei reads 休 'do not' (a prohibitive); here the Ming has 有者 'let be', and the sense is a permission to stay away. Both are the same form; I follow the Ming at each place.

sentences.t: Šiliġün berined ökid-i an-u maqa abčiraγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
perhaps (a particle of tentative suggestion; Ming 莫不 'might it not be that …') [莫不]

words.reading: 阿卜赤舌剌兀勒周 abčiraγ̇ulžu

sentences.l: Comely daughters-in-law, girls(acc), their, perhaps bringing(caus),
sentences.i: Perhaps have their comely daughters-in-law and girls brought,
sentences.n: Another break in a converb chain: the chain abčiraγ̇ulžu … ukijaγ̇ulžu … saγ̇aγ̇ulqun runs over three units. maqa (Ming 莫不) is a particle of tentative suggestion, 'perhaps, might we not'; it recurs in the last unit of §189. The chain ends in saγ̇aγ̇ulqun, a plural imperative ('you all'), so I read the whole chain as advice to Tayang and his men: 'perhaps have them brought, have … washed, have them milk'. ökid-i has the plural -d and the accusative -i, which serve also for berined 'daughters-in-law' (no case ending of its own).

sentences.t: γar köl an-u ukijaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
to wash (stem inferred from the Ming 洗) [敎洗了着]

sentences.l: Hand, foot, their causing-to-wash,
sentences.i: have their hands and feet washed,
sentences.n: ukijaγ̇ulžu: ukija- 'wash' (stem inferred from the Ming 洗) with the causative -γ̇ul-. 'Their' (an-u) points to the girls; the Ming 他的 is the same. The converb is carried into the next unit.

sentences.t: üniġed qonid(i)-jan maqa saγ̇aγ̇ulqun ele" keġežüġüi

morph.gloss: milch cow (Ming 乳牛; stem inferred) [乳牛每]
perhaps (a particle of tentative suggestion; Ming 莫不 'might it not be that …') [莫不]
to milk (stem inferred from the Ming 擠) [敎擠每]

sentences.l: Milch-cows, sheep-own, perhaps causing-to-milk-you, only," saying.
sentences.i: and perhaps have them milk your own cows and sheep. That is all," she said.
sentences.n: saγ̇aγ̇ulqun: saγ̇a- 'milk' (stem inferred from the Ming 擠) with causative -γ̇ul- and the imperative -qun, 'you (all) …' (Ming 每; the printed 每 here may stand for 您). qonid(i)-jan: 'sheep' with plural -d, Shiratori's (i) and the reflexive -jan, 'one's own'; the reflexive follows the subject of the imperative, 'you', so 'your own' ('our own' is possible if she speaks for the household). ele 'only' (Ming 但) ends the speech; the closing mark follows it, and keġežüġüi closes the quotation.

sentences.t: Teġün-dür Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: That-at Tajaṅ Qān, speaking:
sentences.i: Then Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: The same opener as above: teġün-dür, then the speaker, then ügülerün.

sentences.t: "Tein böġesü jaγ̇utan aqun.

morph.gloss: what (the -n drops before the ending) [甚麽(有的)每]

sentences.l: "Thus if-it-be, what-having being.
sentences.i: "If that is so, what do they have?
sentences.n: Tein böġesü, 'so, if it is'; jaγ̇u-tan, 'with what' (the -tan again, Ming 有的每, 'those that have'), aqun 'being' (Ming 有的). The sense 'what have they to show?' is a guess; 'what are they then?' is also possible.

sentences.t: Tede Moṅγol-dur odču qor an-u maqa abčiraja" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
perhaps (a particle of tentative suggestion; Ming 莫不 'might it not be that …') [莫不]

sentences.l: Those, to-Mongols going, quiver their perhaps let-us-bring," saying.
sentences.i: Perhaps we should go to those Mongols and bring away their quivers," he said.
sentences.n: odču 'going' (Ming 去着) is a converb; abčiraja is the hortative, 'let us bring'; maqa (Ming 莫不) as before is tentative, 'perhaps'. The sentence is the plan. qor an-u: 'quiver, their', possessor after the noun.

sentences.t: Edeġer üges-tür Kögseġü-Sabraγ ügülerün:

words.reading: 可克薛兀-撒卜舌剌黑 Kögseġü-Sabraγ

morph.gloss: Kökse'ü-Sabraq, a Naiman man's name [人名]

sentences.l: These words-in Kögseġü-Sabraγ, speaking:
sentences.i: At these words Kökse'ü-Sabraq said:
sentences.n: Edeġer is the plural of ede 'these'; üges-tür is üge 'word' + plural -s + dative-locative -tür (front-vowel form, after s): 'in these words', thus 'at these words'. §190 begins here; the speech it introduces opens with Shiratori's mark before Ai! in the next unit.

sentences.t: "Ai! Jeke üge ügüled ta.

morph.gloss: verb ending with a plural subject (ta); uncertain

sentences.l: "Alas! Great word speaking you.
sentences.i: "Alas! You speak great words.
sentences.n: ügüled is ügüle- + -d, a verb ending that goes with a plural subject (here ta, Ming 您); I note it as uncertain. jeke üge, 'great word', appears again in Belgütei's speech (jeke üge ügülen ažuγ̇u), where it means the Naiman's boasting; here 'great words' may be the same boast, but I leave it unglossed as 'great'.

sentences.t: Ai torluγ Qān žokiqu-ju. bi; niγ̇udqun" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: (sense unknown: the Ming gives no gloss; it stands beside a ruler or a son as an epithet)
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
to be fitting (stem inferred from the Ming 且麽有) [且麽有]
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]
to conceal, hide (stem inferred from the Ming 隱慝; the glossary has niγu-) [(隱慝您)]

sentences.l: Alas! torluγ Qān fitting-?, is; hide-you," saying.
sentences.i: Alas, torluγ Qan, is it fitting? It is so; hide, all of you!" he said.
sentences.n: The least secure line of the part. The Ming reads 唉 (blank) 皇帝 且麽有 有 隱慝您 說了: 'alas, [torluγ], qan, is it fitting?, is, hide-you'. žokiqu-ju is the participle of žoki- 'to suit' with the question particle -ju (as in čidaqu-ju); bi is the short copula, and 'It is so' has no more support than the Ming 有 'is'; niγ̇udqun is niγu- 'conceal' (the glossary's stem; inferred from the Ming 隱慝, which is in brackets, the glossators' own sense) + -d (the ending that goes with a plural subject, as in abčiradqun; uncertain) + the imperative -qun, 'you (all) hide'. The Ming gives no object, so the English gives none ('hide', not 'hide it'). Who is told to hide, and from what, I cannot say; it may mean 'keep it secret' or 'lie low'. torluγ again has no gloss.

sentences.t: Kögseġü-Sebraγ-a idγaγ̇uluγ̇ad bürün Torbi-Taši neretü elči Öṅgüd-ün Alaquši-Digid-Quri-da ügüležü "ilerün

words.reading: 可克薛兀-撒(卜)舌剌中合 Kögseġü-Sebraγ-a

glyphs.s: 可克薛兀-撒(卜)舌剌中合

morph.gloss: dative-locative; with a passive verb, the doer: by

words.reading: 亦惕中合兀魯阿惕 idγaγ̇uluγ̇ad

morph.gloss: to urge, persuade (stem inferred from the Ming 勸) [被勸了]
causative form, but read by the Ming as passive (被)

words.reading: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里-荅 Alaquši-Digid-Quri-da

glyphs.s: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里-荅

sentences.l: Kögseġü-Sebraγ-by being-urged, being, Torbi-Taši named envoy, Öṅgüd's Alaquši-Digid-Quri-to, speaking, "sending:
sentences.i: Urged on by Kökse'ü-Sabraq, he sent an envoy named Torbi-Tashi to Alaqush-Digit-Quri of the Önggüd, saying:
sentences.n: The subject, Tayang, is not restated. Kögseġü-Sebraγ-a (Shiratori writes Sebraγ here) has the dative-locative -a, which with a passive verb names the doer, 'by'; idγaγ̇uluγ̇ad carries the Ming 被勸 'being persuaded' (it has -γ̇ul-, a causative ending, read by the Ming as passive; stem idγa- inferred). Two converbs follow, ügüležü ilerün, 'speaking, when sending'. The print opens a quotation mark before ilerün, not before ene, where the message actually begins; I take it as a slip, and ilerün as the last word of the frame. Öṅgüd-ün is the genitive of the Önggüd, linked to Alaqush-Digit-Quri, not to the envoy.

sentences.t: ene dorona čüġeken Monγol bi keġegdemüi.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (the Ming writes 達達, 'Tatars') [達達]
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: This east few Mongols are, is-said.
sentences.i: "It is said that there are a few Mongols here in the east.
sentences.n: The message repeats Tayang's own words above (Ene dorona čüġeked Monγol bi keġegdemüi) almost word for word, with čüġeken 'few' for čüġeked. Tayang is quoting himself, or the message is the same rumour. See the note there.

sentences.t: Či baraγ̇un γar bol;
sentences.l: You right hand be;
sentences.i: Be my right hand;
sentences.n: baraγ̇un γar, 'right hand' (Ming 右手), is the figure for a trusted helper. bol is the bare stem of bol- 'be, become', an imperative; the semicolon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: bi endēče qamsažu tedeked Moṅγol-un qor an-u abuja" keġežü iležüġü.

morph.gloss: to join, combine (stem inferred from the Ming 併) [併着]
further plural ending (uncertain; Ming 那些 'those few')
their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: I from-here joining, those Mongols' quiver their let-us-take," saying, sent.
sentences.i: I will join from here, and let us take the quivers of those few Mongols," so saying, he sent him.
sentences.n: endēče, from ene 'this' with the ablative -ēče (long vowel), 'from here'. qamsažu: qamsa- 'join' (Ming 併着). abuja is the hortative of ab- 'take' (Ming 要咱). The object, the envoy, is not stated: I follow the glossary's iležüġü 'sent', though the Ming has 去有來, 'went'. The closing mark is after abuja.

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Alaquši-Digid-Quri qariγ̇u ügülerün:

words.reading: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里 Alaquši-Digid-Quri

glyphs.s: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里

sentences.l: That word-in Alaquši-Digid-Quri, answer, speaking:
sentences.i: In reply to that message Alaqush-Digit-Quri said:
sentences.n: tere üge-dür, 'in that word'; qariγ̇u (Ming 囘) is a noun, 'answer', as in the glossary; ügülerün 'speaking' follows it.

sentences.t: "Baraγ̇un γar bolun ülü čidaqu bi" keġežü ileġed
sentences.l: "Right hand being not able I," saying, sent-away.
sentences.i: "I cannot be a right hand," he said, and sent him away.
sentences.n: bolun is the converb of bol- (Ming 做了), ülü negates the participle čidaqu 'able' (Ming 能): 'not able to be'. ileġed is ile- + the converb -ġed, 'having sent' (Ming 敎去了); the chain ends in the next unit with a new action. The object, Tayang's envoy, is not stated.

sentences.t: Alaquši-Digid-Quri Juγunan neretü elči-jer(i)-jen Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a ügüležü ilerün;

words.reading: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里 Alaquši-Digid-Quri

glyphs.s: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里

morph.gloss: instrumental: by means of (front-vowel form of -jar; the token jer(i); uncertain)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Alaquši-Digid-Quri Juγunan named envoy-by-own Čiṅgis Qaγan-to, speaking, sending;
sentences.i: Alaqush-Digit-Quri sent word to Chinggis Qahan by his own envoy, named Juqunan, saying:
sentences.n: elči-jer(i)-jen is the problem word: elči 'envoy', the instrumental -jer (front-vowel form of -jar, which the glossary has in γažar(i)-jar, 'by way of'), Shiratori's (i), and the reflexive -jen 'his own'. So 'by means of his own envoy' (the Ming 使臣自的行 has 自的 for the reflexive and no word for 'by'; uncertain), which suits the verb: word is sent through the envoy. Qaγan-(n)a is the dative-locative 'to Qaγan', with Shiratori's (n). ügüležü ilerün is the same pair as in Tayang's message above. The message begins with a quotation mark before Naiman-u in the next unit.

sentences.t: "Naiman-u Tajaṅ Qān qor čin-ü abura iremüi.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
you (the genitive stem is čin-) [你的]
converb of purpose: in order to take

sentences.l: "Naiman's Tajaṅ Qān quiver your taking comes.
sentences.i: "Tayang Qan of the Naiman is coming to take your quiver.
sentences.n: abura is ab- + the converb of purpose -ura, 'in order to take'. iremüi: ire- 'come' + present -müi. The quiver, qor, is given only as 箭筒 'arrow-case'; what it stands for is left open (see the note on qor(i)-jar(i)-jan above).

sentences.t: Nama-ji baraγ̇un γar bol keġežü iležüġü.

morph.gloss: I (the stem nama- before the accusative) [我行]

sentences.l: Me(acc) right hand be, saying, sent.
sentences.i: He has sent to me, saying, 'Be my right hand.'
sentences.n: nama-ji is bi 'I' in its accusative stem (nama-) with -ji. iležüġü has the Ming 來了有, 'has come', here; I keep 'sent', with Tayang the sender, as in Tayang's message above.

sentences.t: Bi ese bolba.
sentences.l: I not became.
sentences.i: I did not become his right hand.
sentences.n: ese (Ming 不曾) negates a past action, here with bolba (bol- 'become' + -ba). 'I did not become his right hand' keeps to the grammar: the thing that was not 'become' is the right hand he was asked to be (compare 'I cannot be a right hand' above). The sense is a refusal, which I leave to the reader.

sentences.t: Edöġe bi čima-da sereġülžü ilebe. irežü qor(i)-jan abdaγ̇užai či" keġežü iležüġüi.

morph.gloss: you (the stem čima- before the dative) [你 行]
to be aware, be on guard (stem inferred from the Ming 省) [敎省着]
apprehensive ending: lest (Ming 恐 'for fear that')

sentences.l: Now I you-to causing-to-be-aware sent. Coming, quiver-own may-be-taken you," saying, sent.
sentences.i: Now I have sent to make you watchful, lest he come and your own quiver be taken from you." So saying, he sent.
sentences.n: sereġülžü: sere- 'be aware' (stem inferred from the Ming 省) with the causative and the converb. abdaγ̇užai, from ab- 'take' with passive -da- and the ending -γ̇užai, Ming 恐被要了 'for fear it be taken': a warning, 'lest'. The reflexive qor(i)-jan, 'one's own quiver', refers to či, 'you', at the end of the clause. The closing mark is after či; keġežü iležüġüi, 'saying, sent', ends the message.

sentences.t: Žöb tende Čiṅgis Qaγan Temeġen-Keġer-i abakažu Tülkin-Čeġüd-i qomorču büküi-dür

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to hold a circle hunt (stem inferred from the Ming 圍獵; compare aba) [圍獵着]
to close in, encircle (stem inferred from the Ming 圍合) [圍合着]

sentences.l: Right, there Čiṅgis Qaγan Temeġen-Keġer(acc) circle-hunting, Tülkin-Čeġüd(acc) enclosing, at-being,
sentences.i: Just then, while Chinggis Qahan was holding a circle hunt at Teme'en-Ke'er and closing in on Tülkin-Che'üd,
sentences.n: žöb tende, 'right, there', is 'just then' (Ming 是 那裏; the glossary notes 'just then' elsewhere). Temeġen-Keġer-i and Tülkin-Čeġüd-i, with the accusative -i, are place names (Ming 地名行); the English spelling of both is mine. abakažu is a converb from a stem inferred from the Ming 圍獵, 'circle-hunt', and aba 'the hunt'; qomorču, 'enclosing' (Ming 圍合着). büküi-dür is the participle bü-küi + -dür, 'when being'.

sentences.t: Alaquši-Digid-Quri-jin ilegsen Juγunan elči ene kelen kürgen irebe.

words.reading: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里-因 Alaquši-Digid-Quri-jin

glyphs.s: 阿剌中忽石-的吉惕-中忽舌里-因

morph.gloss: Alaqush-Digit-Quri, a man's name [人名 的]

sentences.l: Alaquši-Digid-Quri's sent Juγunan envoy this word bringing came.
sentences.i: the envoy Juqunan, sent by Alaqush-Digit-Quri, came with this word.
sentences.n: ilegsen is the participle of ile- 'send' used as an adjective before the envoy. kürgen is kürge- 'bring' (a causative of kür- 'reach', uncertain) + the converb -n, 'bringing' (Ming 到). kelen (Ming 話) is 'word, speech'.

sentences.t: Ene kelen-dür aba deġere böġed ker kikün keġeldüġesü olon küġün ügülerün:

morph.gloss: converb, 'being so'; also a particle of sequence (Ming 便 'at once, then')

sentences.l: This word-in hunt on being, how shall-do, if-saying-to-one-another, many person speaking:
sentences.i: At this news, while on the hunt, when they conferred on what to do, many men said:
sentences.n: keġeldüġesü is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + the conditional -ġesü: 'if / when they said to one another', Ming 共說呵 'say together'. aba deġere böġed: 'on the hunt, being so' (Ming 圍獵上 便), taken as 'while still on the hunt', uncertain. kikün is the future participle 'shall do' (ker kikün 'how shall we do?').

sentences.t: "Aγtas bidan-u turuγad bi.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (the stem takes -n- before the ending)
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: "Geldings of-us lean are.
sentences.i: "Our geldings are lean.
sentences.n: aγtas is aγta 'gelding' with the plural -s (Ming 騸馬每); turuγad is turuγ 'lean' with plural -ad (Ming 痩每). bi 'are' (Ming 有) is not supplied in the literal.

sentences.t: Edöġe jakikün bida" keġeldüžüġüi.
sentences.l: Now what-shall-do we," consulted-together.
sentences.i: What shall we do now?" they said to one another.
sentences.n: The closing mark is after bida; keġeldüžüġüi is the past of the same reciprocal keġeldü- 'speak to one another' that we saw above. jakikün: jaki- 'do what' + -kün, 'what shall we do?'.

sentences.t: Teġün-dür Ödčigin nojan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]

sentences.l: That-at Ödčigin noyan, speaking:
sentences.i: Then the noyan Ödchigin said:
sentences.n: nojan 'lord' (Ming 官人) follows the name as a title; Ödčigin is a name (Ming 人名), my English spelling Ödchigin.

sentences.t: "Aγtas turuγad keġen jakin šiltaγdaqu.

morph.gloss: to make an excuse, plead (stem inferred from the Ming 推辭) [推辭]

sentences.l: "Geldings lean saying, how making-excuse?
sentences.i: "Why plead that the geldings are lean?
sentences.n: keġen 'saying' (Ming 麽道) closes the pleading, so 'geldings lean' is what is being said by the others. šiltaγdaqu is the participle of šiltaγda- 'make an excuse' (stem inferred from the Ming 推辭), with jakin 'how, why' before it.

sentences.t: Min-u aγtas tarγud bi.

morph.gloss: I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: My geldings fat are.
sentences.i: My geldings are fat.
sentences.n: min-u aγtas, 'my geldings'; tarγud 'fat' (Ming 肥每) with plural -d; no copula.

sentences.t: Eimü üges sonosču jakin saγ̇uγdaqu" keġebe.
sentences.l: Such words hearing, how be-seated?" said.
sentences.i: Hearing such words, how can we sit still?" he said.
sentences.n: saγ̇uγdaqu: saγ̇u- 'sit' + -γda- (passive? Ming 可坐 'is it fit to sit') + the participle: 'how can one sit?'. The closing mark is after it, ending Ödčigin's speech, which began at 'Aγtas'.

sentences.t: Basa Belgütei nojan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Belgütei noyan, speaking:
sentences.i: Then the noyan Belgütei spoke in turn:
sentences.n: basa 'again, also' (Ming 再). The same form as above: name, nojan, ügülerün.

sentences.t: "Amitu böġetele nökör-e qor(i)-jan abdaγ̇asu aγsan jaγ̇un tusa bi.

morph.gloss: dative-locative; with a passive verb, the doer: by
past participle: the one who is
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: "Living being-while, companion-to quiver-own if-taken, the-living what use is.
sentences.i: "While we live, if our own quiver is taken by a follower, what use is our living?
sentences.n: nökör-e, 'to a companion', is the doer of the passive abdaγ̇asu, 'if it is taken' (Ming 被要了呵), so 'by a follower'. qor(i)-jan, 'one's own quiver', refers back to a general subject. aγsan, from a- 'be, live' (Ming 活的, 'the living one'), jaγ̇un tusa bi is 'what use is there?'. I read the point as rhetorical, a disgrace to be disarmed by one's own man; the text does not say 'disgrace'.

sentences.t: Töregsen ere-de üküġesü taki
sentences.l: Born man-to if-dies also,
sentences.i: When a man who was born dies, too,
sentences.n: töregsen, past participle 'the one born'; ere-de, 'to the man'; üküġesü, conditional 'if he dies'. taki 'also' (Ming 也). This and the next unit are one sentence: the condition is here, the consequence follows.

sentences.t: qor numun- lüġe-ben jasun-luγ̇a nigen-(n)e kebteġesü ülü-ü sain bi.

morph.gloss: bow (Ming 弓弩; the hyphen is the printer's, at a line end) [弓]
is, there is (short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: Quiver, bow with-own bone-with one-in if-lying not good is.
sentences.i: is it not good to lie in one place, his quiver and bow with him, together with his bones?
sentences.n: numun- carries a hyphen at the line end (Ming 弓弩門-), which the print leaves in the word. lüġe-ben is 'with his own' (lüġe + reflexive -ben); jasun-luγ̇a is 'with the bone'. ülü-ü sain bi: ülü-ü (Ming 不) with the particle -ü, which may make the question, 'is it not good?'; the Ming here puts no 麽 on it, so the question is a guess from the sense.

sentences.t: Naiman irgen ulus jeketü irge olotu keġen jeke üge ügülen ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: many (the -n drops before the ending) [多有的]

sentences.l: Naiman people realm great-having, people many-having saying, great word speaking was.
sentences.i: Saying, 'The Naiman are a people with a great realm and many subjects,' they were speaking great words.
sentences.n: keġen closes the Naiman's boast. jeketü and olotu are -tu/-tü possessives, Ming 大有的 and 多有的, 'having greatness, having many'. The subject of ažuγ̇u 'was' is the Naiman, unstated; ügülen ažuγ̇u is a converb + auxiliary 'was speaking'. irge is a variant of irgen (Ming 百姓 for both).

sentences.t: Bida ene an-u jeke üge-dür šiqan morilažu odču an-u qor abuγ̇asu berkedü-ü ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
to press close, lean on (stem inferred; Ming 倚 'lean') [倚着]
their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: We this their great word-on pressing, mounting, going, their quiver if-taking hard-? was.
sentences.i: Pressing on those great words of theirs, if we mount, ride out and take their quiver, would that be hard?
sentences.n: šiqan (Ming 倚着, 'leaning on') I read as 'pressing hard on', i.e. calling their bluff; the stem šiqa- is inferred and the sense is a guess. morilažu is mori(n) 'horse' with the verbal -la- and the converb. abuγ̇asu is the conditional of ab- 'take' (Ming 要呵), and the chain šiqan morilažu odču … abuγ̇asu leads up to it, so the whole is 'if, pressing …, we mount, go and take'; the next unit begins with oduγ̇asu, the conditional of od- 'go' (去呵). berkedü-ü has the question particle -ü (Ming 麽), 'hard?'; ažuγ̇u (Ming 有來) I render in the present, as a rhetorical 'would it be?'.

sentences.t: Oduγ̇asu olon aduγ̇un an-u žoγsažu ülü-ü qočoruγ̇užai.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
to rest (stem inferred from the Ming 歇息) [歇息着]
to fall behind, be left behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後麽]

sentences.l: If-going many herd their resting not fall-behind-?
sentences.i: If we go, will their many herds, resting, not be left behind?
sentences.n: Three parallel questions follow in this speech (this unit and the next two), each with ülü-ü and an ending in -užai, Ming 落後麽 / 上去麽. I read the ending as 'might … not?' and qočoru- as 'fall behind, be left behind' (inferred from the Ming 落後); the sense is that the Naiman will be in disorder when attacked: herds, camps, people. The reading is uncertain throughout.

sentences.t: Ordo ger an-u eġürežü ülü-ü qočoruγ̇užai.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
to empty (the Ming glosses it in brackets, (空着); stem inferred) [(空着)]
to fall behind, be left behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後麽]

sentences.l: Palace, house their emptying not fall-behind-?
sentences.i: Will their palace and house, emptied, not be left behind?
sentences.n: ordo ger an-u: 'palace, house, their' (Ming 宮, 室), a pair for a lord's household. eġürežü is Ming (空着), glossed in brackets: 'emptied'. For qočoruγ̇užai see the previous unit.

sentences.t: olon ulus an-u ündür etüged-tür qorura ülü-ü γaruγ̇užai.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
earth, ground, land (the glossary has the name Etügen, 'the Earth') [處裏]
plural (uncertain; the Ming 處 does not mark it)
to shelter, take refuge (stem inferred from the Ming 躱避) [躱避]
converb of purpose: in order to (as in abura)
to go up, go out (stem inferred from the Ming 上去) [上去麽]

sentences.l: Many people their high places-in sheltering not go-up-?
sentences.i: Will their many people not go up to the high places for shelter?
sentences.n: olon ulus an-u, 'many people their'. etüged-tür is etügen 'earth, ground, land' (the glossary has the name Etügen, 'the Earth'; the Ming 處 says 'place'), the plural -d (uncertain: the Ming does not mark it) and -tür; ündür 'high' stands before it. qorura (Ming 躱避, 'hide, shelter') I take as qoru- with the converb of purpose -ra, as in abura above, 'in order to shelter'; the stem is inferred. γaruγ̇užai 'go up' (Ming 上去麽) ends the same pattern as in the two units above.

sentences.t: Müd ene eimü jeke üge üġüleġülžü ker saγ̇uγdaqu" morilaja böġed" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to speak (a spelling of ügüle-) [敎說着]
converb, 'being so'; also a particle of sequence (Ming 便 'at once, then')

sentences.l: They this such great word causing-to-speak, how be-seated?" let-us-mount, then," said.
sentences.i: They have let such great words be spoken; how can we sit still? Let us mount at once," he said.
sentences.n: Müd is 'they' (Ming 他每). üġüleġülžü is a causative of ügüle- 'speak' (Ming 敎說着, 'causing to say'); the subject is the Naiman, who 'had such great words said' — boasted. morilaja is the hortative 'let us mount'; böġed (Ming 便) 'then, at once'. The print has a closing mark after saγ̇uγdaqu and another after böġed; I give only the second in the English, as the end of Belgütei's speech, and leave the first (it may end the complaint about the Naiman's words, with the call to mount after it; uncertain). keġebe closes the frame.
